documents.title: Same-day request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt calling before work. Two days of burning, frequency and lower belly ache, says it feels exactly like November. No fever, no back pain, no vomiting. Not pregnant per pt, period was a couple weeks ago. Offered 12:40 (her lunch block); accepted. Asked her to bring a urine sample or come in able to give one.

medications.drug: nitrofurantoin, macrocrystals 25 MG / nitrofurantoin, monohydrate 75 MG Oral Capsule
medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily with food for 5 days

results.test: Bacteria in Urine sediment by Microscopy high power field

results.text: Escherichia coli, 50,000-100,000 CFU/mL. Susceptible to nitrofurantoin.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Acute Visit - Urinary Symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 y/o F with recurrent UTIs.

HPI: Since Saturday, painful urination, frequency and a dull ache above the pubic bone. By her count this is the third bout in about a year: April (urgent care), November here (culture E. coli, treated with nitrofurantoin), and now. No fever, rigors or flank pain. Denies discharge, genital lesions, or any new partner; same partner, condoms used inconsistently. LMP about two weeks ago, normal.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal (see flowsheet). Nontoxic. Abdomen soft, tender suprapubically, no rebound. No CVA tenderness.

UA today: LE 2+, nitrite +, blood neg; WBC 35/hpf, RBC 2/hpf, many bacteria.

Assessment: acute cystitis, recurrent pattern. Prior culture E. coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin.

Plan:
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily x 5 days.
- Urine culture sent; will adjust if resistant.
- Hydration, void after intercourse.
- Call for fever, flank pain, vomiting, or no improvement in 2 days.

documents.title: Culture back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Culture grew E. coli again, sensitive to what you're taking. Keep going through the full course. How are the symptoms?

documents.title: RE: Culture back
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Totally fine now, done with the antibiotic yesterday. Thanks.

documents.title: Scheduling
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Is it time for my yearly checkup? Kids come back next week so anything after 3:15 works best.

documents.title: RE: Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Yes, you're due. You're booked Monday 9/8 at 3:30. No fasting needed.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 28 y/o teacher, school year just started, feels good.

Interval: no UTIs since the February episode. No urinary symptoms now. No other illnesses, no ED or urgent care visits.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Social unchanged: never smoker, 1-2 drinks a month, same partner.
PHQ-2 = 0.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: BP and vitals on flowsheet, normal. Weight steady. Eyes, ears, throat normal. No lymphadenopathy, thyroid normal. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Extremities normal. Skin: no worrisome lesions. Neuro grossly intact.

Assessment and plan:
- Recurrent UTIs: quiet since February. Same-day visits with a urine sample remain the plan if symptoms recur.
- Last Tdap 2009 per old records: Tdap given today.
- Pap from 2023 normal, due next year.
- Labs from last fall all normal; nothing needed today.
- Flu and COVID vaccines in October at a nurse visit.
Follow up next year.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days

documents.title: External fill history
documents.author: MA
documents.body: External prescription history import flagged a new fill: metronidazole 500 mg tablets, #14, 1 tab twice daily, filled 10/13/2025. Prescriber is an outside gynecologist. No visit note from that office on file. Added to med list as an outside short course; routing to PCP.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Here for flu and updated COVID shots. Feels well, afebrile. Asked about the metronidazole that showed up on her fill history: she went to her gynecologist last week for discharge with an odor and was told it was a bacterial imbalance (BV). Finished the 7 days yesterday, avoided alcohol while on it, symptoms gone. No urinary symptoms.

Flu (trivalent) IM L deltoid, COVID-19 updated mRNA IM R deltoid. VIS reviewed. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction.

Records request faxed to the gynecology office for the 10/13 visit.

documents.title: Records request follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called the gynecology office about our 10/21 records request. Their records person said it's in the queue; re-faxed the signed release at their request. Will check again.
